players.product: AI data-center leasing at Rockdale and Corsicana, Texas (Tier III build-to-suit on in-place utility power; AMD 50 MW, frontier AI lab 191 MW)

quarterly_data.signal: 8-K (Item 8.01 / release): the Data Center Lease and Services Agreement with the unnamed leading frontier AI lab has an initial 20-year term running through June 2048 and an estimated average annual NOI contribution of $365 to $411 million; delivery is phased (Phase 1 of 96 IT MW in December 2027, Phase 2 of 95 MW by June 2028) on Riot's existing, fully approved interconnection at Rockdale. The earnings deck says the tenant's basis of design is incorporated with full design and internal architecture completed, preferred delivery partners of this tenant are engaged, required power availability is secured, and ESS Metron and E4A capabilities are integrated into the delivery plan to accelerate substation development and reduce long-lead equipment risk.
quarterly_data.figure: lease through June 2048; average annual NOI $365 to $411 million; Phase 2 95 MW June 2028

quarterly_data.signal: 8-K earnings deck: of Q2 2026 Data Center revenue, $18.3 million was tenant fit-out services revenue at a 13% gross margin (procurement and installation of customer-specific equipment, reimbursed by the tenant on a cost-plus basis) and base rent was $4.5 million at a 91% gross margin; Data Center gross profit was $6.5 million (28%). In Q1 2026 Data Center revenue was $33.2 million, of which tenant fit-out services $32.2 million.
quarterly_data.figure: tenant fit-out $18.3 million (13%); base rent $4.5 million (91%); data center gross profit $6.5 million (28%)

quarterly_data.signal: 8-K earnings deck: since acquiring ESS Metron in December 2021, Riot has realized $23.8M in cumulative capex savings; Q2 2026 Engineering gross profit was $10,256 thousand (27.5% margin) on revenue of $37,286 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: $23.8M cumulative capex savings; Q2 engineering gross profit $10,256 thousand (27.5%)

quarterly_data.signal: 8-K earnings deck (Q2 2026 by the numbers): approximately 1,700 MW of available total power capacity in Texas and 300 MW in Kentucky.
quarterly_data.figure: ~1,700 MW available power capacity in Texas; 300 MW in Kentucky
